ai_summary:
Scotland’s clean generation continues to illustrate deep transmission bottlenecks across the British electricity network. Great Britain's total wind output currently stands at 6.0 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output providing 3.1 GW, which represents 30.7% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This robust local generation suppresses Scottish carbon intensity to an exceptionally clean 5 gCO2/kWh, standing in stark contrast to the GB-wide average of 173 gCO2/kWh.

Due to boundary export limitations, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 5,381 MWh, incurring a direct balancing constraint cost of about £172,680. Because this clean power could not reach southern demand centres, an estimated 1,022,409 cubic meters of fossil gas had to be burned elsewhere to balance the grid, releasing an avoidable 1,883 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere.

Extrapolating today’s run-rate, the total yearly cost of curtailment is estimated at £63 million. Socialised across consumer electricity bills through national balancing charges, this structural transmission barrier increases everybody's invoice in the UK by an estimated £0.2/MWh, underlining the pressing economic and environmental case for accelerated grid infrastructure investment.
